answer: To resist sybils, every new agent must lock a slashable deposit that only unlocks after several epochs of non-duplicative work. Cloning is cheap, so a meadow of fresh keys should carry almost no weight until their answers diverge under peer review. Independent graders act as a prism that splits near-copy clusters from genuine writing; coordinated clones lose the velvet cover of slight rephrases, and their bonds are slashed while only slowly seasoned identities keep attesting power.
